transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Emily (Redwood SE), Diego (CSM), Jamal (Aurelia Infra), Priya (ML), Laura (Security), Markus (Cloud), Nina (PM)

(00:00) Samir (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick roll call and then we'll go into the telemetry.
(00:18) Jamal: hey, present. Priya here. Laura and Markus are on.
(00:28) Emily (SE): cool, i'll start with a quick telemetry overview - i'll share screen after this link: https://app.redwood.ai/pilot/bench/ORCH-8421
(00:45) Priya: perfect, we saw a spike in our tail p99 starting thursday night, just want to understand root cause.
(01:05) Emily: right - summary is during long-form medical note generation sequences we observed p99 jump from ~420ms to ~900ms for a subset of requests. avg stayed stable.
(01:30) Markus: was that for the same model variant? we have mixed quantization profiles in the pool.
(01:42) Emily: yes mostly the 8-bit quantized variant, but interestingly we saw the regressed traces hitting node pool B which is running kernel set v1.11.3, whereas the other pool is on v1.11.7.
(02:05) Jamal: hmm nodes did do a rolling reboot early friday, maybe kube-scheduler contended. we also had a flurry of batch imports overnight.
(02:28) Emily: logs show increased KV cache miss rates for a subset of prefixes - might be an eviction pattern when concurrency spikes. note: KV cache logged as "KV cash" in some syslogs so ignore spelling in the dump.
(02:55) Samir: is that a config problem or a kernel regression?
(03:12) Emily: leaning kernel-related because the same workload on v1.11.7 didn't show the same miss pattern. could be allocation change in the attention kernel.
(03:35) Priya: can we reproduce in test? we'd prefer a quick repro harness vs guessing.
(03:55) Emily: yes - plan is to run a targeted microbenchmark that reproduces long-context hits and measure p50/p95/p99 across kernels and quant profiles. i'll run that against pool B and pool A and share results.
(04:20) Nina (PM): timeline for that? we need to update execs by tuesday.
(04:28) Emily: i can have initial numbers by thursday EOD, finalized by friday.
(04:40) Diego (CSM): i'll collate and highlight risky regressions for the canary plan.
(04:50) Laura (Security): quick sec question - any change in KV storage encryption or KMS calls with the new orchestrator? audit needs to know.
(05:10) Emily: no changes to encryption semantics in the 1.12.0 orchestrator, but some calls moved to async KMS flow to reduce tail latency. we'll document exact KMS call graph.
(05:35) Laura: async KMS flow is ok but we need audit events for success/failure and key id mapping.
(05:50) Samir: noted - we'll add a doc snippet. Samir to follow up on audit fields.
(06:10) Jamal: another observation - egress shaping rules on our edge NAT were tightened last week, might have introduced bursts when rules hit connection limits.
(06:28) Markus: yes we did a rollout to block noisy egress flows, might have affected upstream TCP windows.
(06:40) Emily: please share the egress ACLs, and we'll correlate with connection resets in our tracer.
(06:55) Jamal: will upload 72h logs to the shared bucket - link will be posted in the pilot channel.
(07:15) Samir: on routing - we ran the fallback experiment routing certain slow requests to a lower-cost model variant. results?
(07:30) Priya: good results for cost, but quality dropped for some note types. we need to tighten the decision rule.
(07:45) Emily: suggestion: add a request classifier that sends only high-entropy prompts to the full model, others to quantized variant. we can bake that into the routing policy as a pre-filter.
(08:05) Nina: classifier adds latency though, correct?
(08:18) Emily: negligible if it's a light-weight embedding or heuristic; we can do it in <20ms. tradeoff vs saving ~30% token cost.
(08:35) Priya: ok worth trying. can the routing be changed without redeploying the private control plane?
(08:48) Samir: yes, routing rules are config-driven; we can push a canary rule to 10% traffic. that's in the canary playbook.
(09:05) Markus: about the orchestrator 1.12.0 upgrade - what's the visible impact window?
(09:18) Emily: upgrade includes kernel selector improvements, better batching heuristics, and a new memory reclaim path. planned canary next wednesday, full roll over the weekend if stable.
(09:38) Jamal: downtime?
(09:45) Emily: no user-visible downtime expected; there's a graceful drain, but we'll run low-traffic windows and have automatic rollback.
(10:05) Laura: need to see rollback steps and who has permission to initiate. R-B-A-C details please.
(10:22) Samir: Samir to send the rollback playbook and list of roles that can trigger it.
(10:35) Priya: regarding telemetry - can we get token-level traces lifted into our Splunk?
(10:48) Diego: we can export trace snippets; full token logs are sensitive but we can sample and redact.
(11:05) Priya: sampling will be fine if we keep fidelity on error cases.
(11:18) Emily: will put together a sampling plan and a mapping doc for SpanIDs -> request IDs.
(11:35) Jamal: any other gotchas you folks saw in similar pilots?
(11:45) Emily: watch out for Nagle/MTU mismatches across hybrid links; that can produce weird tail effects for small token batches. also quantized model scheduling can be starved if sizing is not balanced.
(12:10) Markus: one more item - cloud provider bumped ephemeral disk I/O on some nodes - we saw a brief spike correlated with our checkpoint writes.
(12:28) Samir: ok that may explain some of the Friday noise. Jamal, please include disk metrics in the upload.
(12:50) Laura: on compliance, we have a few SOC 2 scope questions: retention windows, KMS key lifecycle, and export controls for PHI.
(13:10) Samir: we'll loop in our security PM and send the SOC2 scoping doc; Samir to attach the redwood public SOC2 artifact and a private addendum for pilot.
(13:32) Nina: timeline recap?
(13:38) Emily: bench run results by 2026-11-26, canary plan + rollback by 2026-11-25, security scoping doc by 2026-11-30.
(13:55) Samir: ok, good recap. any final questions?
(14:10) Priya: can Emily include raw traces for two failing requests so our model team can review?
(14:20) Emily: yes will include minimum necessary redacted traces.
(14:35) Jamal: i'll upload egress logs by EOD tomorrow.
(14:50) Samir: great thanks all, we'll follow up in the pilot slack channel and post the artifacts.
(15:00) Diego: thanks everyone, bye.

End of transcript.
